adversarial_audit.challenge: POVM completeness might forbid a zero target-success coordinate.
adversarial_audit.response: Completeness fixes only the seed diagonal. The PSD Gram off-diagonals create exact destructive cancellation.

adversarial_audit.challenge: A constant decoder success might disappear asymptotically.
adversarial_audit.response: The Poisson limit gives an explicit positive constant for every fixed rejected multiplicity.

adversarial_audit.challenge: Random signed/unit transforms can move a hard target to an easy one.
adversarial_audit.response: They preserve fiber cardinality exactly, and the counterexample accepts or rejects whole multiplicity strata.

adversarial_audit.challenge: The counterexample is itself an efficient DCP decoder.
adversarial_audit.response: No. It is multiplicity-table dependent and only refutes an information-theoretic per-target inference.

claim_gate.reason: A valid covariant POVM can have constant decoding success while its witness filter vanishes on a positive-mass multiplicity stratum, and natural witness-bijection orbits preserve that stratum.

falsifiers_triggered: POVM completeness constrains the diagonal seed but does not force every cleaned target coefficient to be nonzero.
Constant average DCP decoding success does not imply inverse-polynomial success for every legal subset-sum target.
Signed, permuted, and odd-unit self-reductions preserve target multiplicity and cannot cross the counterexample's rejected stratum.
The multiplicity-aware counterexample is not efficiently implementable and is not a quantum algorithm.
The existing average measurement-to-witness reduction remains valid and is not weakened by this boundary.

proof_obligations.resolution: The root-of-unity Gram construction is PSD with unit diagonal and cyclic twirl equal to identity.
Equal rejected amplitudes cancel, yielding q=0 there and q=1 on every accepted legal target.
The zero-truncated Poisson law gives every fixed stratum positive legal mass and the accepted amplitude a positive limit.
Those witness-bijection transformations preserve exact multiplicity, so they cannot leave the rejected stratum.
The construction consumes the full multiplicity table and is deliberately not promoted to an algorithm.

summary: Covariance and natural DCP instance symmetries cannot upgrade the average witness reduction to every legal target: an exact constant-success POVM can reject an entire positive-mass multiplicity stratum.

theorem.cleaned_filter_statement: the arbitrary-measurement inverse has q_s=1 off the rejected stratum and q_s=0 on it
theorem.consequence: covariance, completeness, and natural instance randomization do not upgrade average legal-target witness success to every target
theorem.correlation_seed_construction: C is the Gram matrix of e_0 on accepted targets and root-of-unity phases times e_1 on one equal-amplitude multiplicity stratum
theorem.density_one_limit: for fixed j, rejected uniform-legal mass tends to 1/(j!(e-1)) while decoder success tends to a positive constant
theorem.exact_povm_statement: C>=0 and diag(C)=1, so E_0=C/N and its cyclic translates sum to I
theorem.natural_orbit_invariant: coordinate permutations/complements and odd-unit multiplication are witness bijections and preserve c_s exactly
theorem.scope_limit: The multiplicity-aware seed is not shown efficiently implementable. The result blocks an information-theoretic proof strategy, not efficient per-target reductions using new non-orbit structure.

theorem_contract.dependency: quenched Poisson fiber law proved in the existing uniform-legal multiplicity module
theorem_contract.ensemble: density-one cyclic DCP phase ensemble on legal fibers
theorem_contract.measurement_class: all exact covariant POVMs at the information-theoretic level
theorem_contract.scope: The multiplicity-aware seed is not shown efficiently implementable. The result blocks an information-theoretic proof strategy, not efficient per-target reductions using new non-orbit structure.
